generations: When big-city event planner Josie Marlowe is sent to tiny Pottersville, Kansas, to shut down her late grandmother's struggling farm before Easter, she expects a quick weekend of paperwork. Instead, she collides with Sam Hollis, the stubborn local veterinarian and egg-hunt organizer, who needs the farm's fields to save the town's beloved 50-year-old Easter festival. Forced to team up after a snowstorm strands them together, the two clash over everything from fence repairs to a runaway flock of rescued chickens, all while trading barbs that slowly turn into flirtation. As Josie rediscovers her roots through church potlucks, sunrise services, and her grandmother's hidden recipe box, she begins to question the polished life waiting for her back in Chicago. On Easter morning, just as the festival succeeds and a job offer pulls her away, Josie makes a grand gesture of her own by staying, and she and Sam share a kiss among pastel eggs and wildflowers.

When big-city event planner Maggie Doyle inherits her late grandmother's failing egg farm in Buttercup, Kansas, she arrives two weeks before Easter planning to sell it fast. The town insists she honor her grandmother's tradition of hosting the annual Easter egg hunt, and the only person who can help is Caleb Turner, the stubborn local veterinarian who has secretly been keeping the farm's hens alive. As the two clash over everything from decorations to dyeing methods, they start working side by side, and Maggie begins to rediscover the warmth of the community she left behind. Just as sparks fly during a thunderstorm rescue of a stranded lamb, Maggie's real estate buyer arrives early with a lucrative offer, and Caleb learns she had planned to sell all along. On Easter morning, Maggie tears up the contract in front of the entire town, and the movie ends with her and Caleb sharing a kiss as the children scramble across the fields to find the golden egg.

When big-city event planner Maggie Collins is sent to tiny Pickett Creek, Kansas, to shut down her late grandmother's struggling farm before Easter, she expects a quick weekend of paperwork. Instead, she collides with Cal Brenner, the stubborn neighboring farmer and volunteer organizer of the town's beloved Easter egg hunt, who insists the farm is the heart of the celebration. After a series of mishaps involving runaway goats, a flooded pasture, and a disastrous attempt at baking her grandmother's famous hot cross buns, Maggie begins to fall for both the town and Cal. Just as the two share a long-awaited kiss at the sunrise Easter service, Maggie's boss arrives with a buyer, and Cal discovers she had been hiding the real reason for her visit. Heartbroken but inspired, Maggie uses her professional skills to turn the Easter hunt into a huge community festival that saves the farm, then races back from the city to join Cal under the blooming redbuds for a happily-ever-after ending.

When big-city pastry chef Maggie Doyle inherits her late grandmother's failing bakery in tiny Pleasant Creek, Kansas, she plans to sell it quickly and return to Chicago before Easter. Her plans get complicated by Jake Whitaker, a stubborn local farmer and the town's volunteer Easter festival organizer, who insists she must bake the traditional 500-person egg hunt cakes as her grandmother always did. Reluctantly, Maggie agrees, and the two clash over everything from her fancy recipes to his refusal to change a single festival tradition. As they work side by side through muddy fields, flour-covered kitchens, and one disastrous runaway-lamb incident, their bickering slowly turns into genuine affection. Just as they share a kiss on the eve of the festival, Maggie receives a dream job offer in Paris, but after the egg hunt, she realizes that home is where her heart is and decides to stay and reopen the bakery with Jake by her side.

When big-city event planner Maggie Doyle inherits her late grandmother's struggling farm in tiny Buttercup, Kansas, she plans to sell it quickly, but she arrives just days before the town's legendary Easter egg hunt. The hunt's longtime organizer, widowed veterinarian Sam Whitaker, reluctantly accepts her help after the church committee insists the farm host this year's event, as it has for generations. Between chasing runaway lambs, battling a sabotaging rival bakery owner, and accidentally getting the town's prized Easter ham stolen by a goat, Maggie and Sam bicker their way into an undeniable spark. Just as they share a heartfelt kiss at the sunrise church service, Sam discovers Maggie has already signed paperwork with a developer, and he storms off feeling betrayed. On Easter morning, Maggie tears up the contract, rallies the whole town to save the hunt, and wins Sam's heart as hundreds of pastel eggs and a very guilty goat cap off a happily-ever-after.

When big-city event planner Josie Marlowe is sent to tiny Pickett Springs, Kansas, to shut down her late grandmother's struggling farm before Easter, she expects a quick weekend of paperwork and goodbyes. Instead, she's roped into running the town's beloved Easter egg hunt by Cal Brennan, the charming, stubborn local veterinarian who has been secretly keeping her grandmother's farm afloat. Their clashing styles, her spreadsheets versus his "we've always done it this way" approach, lead to a chaotic week of runaway goats, a sabotaged pie contest, and an unexpected spark under the prairie stars. Just as Josie begins to fall for both Cal and the town, he discovers her company plans to sell the land to developers, and he feels betrayed that she never told him. On Easter morning, Josie turns down her promotion, rallies the community to save the farm with the best egg hunt Pickett Springs has ever seen, and wins Cal back with a kiss among the wildflowers.

When big-city event planner Maddie Collins is sent to the tiny town of Pleasant Bluff, Kansas, to shut down her late grandmother's struggling farm, she arrives just days before the town's beloved Easter egg festival. She immediately clashes with Jake Henderson, the stubborn local veterinarian and festival organizer, who needs her grandmother's pasture to host the event and refuses to let her sell. To prove she can't be bothered with small-town traditions, Maddie reluctantly agrees to help him pull off the festival, only to find herself falling for the quirky neighbors, the sunrise church services, and Jake's habit of rescuing runaway lambs. Just as sparks fly during a flour-dusted pie-baking disaster, Maddie's boss announces a buyer who plans to bulldoze the land, forcing her to choose between her career and the life she never knew she wanted. On Easter morning, Maddie turns down the deal, rallies the town to save the farm, and shares a kiss with Jake in a field of hidden pastel eggs as the whole community cheers.

When big-city event planner Maddie Collins is sent to tiny Pickett Creek, Kansas, to shut down her late grandmother's struggling farm before Easter, she expects a quick weekend of paperwork. Instead, she runs into Jake Holloway, the stubborn local veterinarian and her grandmother's neighbor, who is determined to keep the farm alive and is secretly in charge of the town's beloved annual Easter egg hunt. After a mishap involving a runaway goat and a flooded church basement, Maddie reluctantly agrees to help Jake save the festival, and their bickering slowly gives way to flirtation among the pastel-decorated barns and potluck dinners. Just as sparks fly during a moonlit night of dyeing eggs, Jake discovers Maddie's boss plans to sell the land to a developer, and he feels betrayed that she never told him. On Easter morning, Maddie tears up the sale agreement, rallies the whole town to pull off the biggest egg hunt in Kansas history, and wins Jake's heart with a heartfelt apology and a decision to stay in Pickett Creek for good.

When big-city pastry chef Maddie Rhodes is fired days before Easter, she retreats to her tiny hometown of Plum Creek, Kansas, where her grandmother's struggling diner is about to host the annual Easter Egg Extravaganza. There she butts heads with Cole Tanner, a stubborn local farmer and the event's overworked organizer, who thinks she's only back to sell the diner and escape again. Forced to team up when a storm wipes out the town's egg-hunt field and the church's brunch supplies, the two stage a chaotic, barn-based celebration with hand-dyed eggs, borrowed lambs, and a rogue goat who steals the show. Amid late-night pie baking, tractor-side confessions, and one near-kiss interrupted by that goat, Maddie realizes she's rediscovering the home she thought she'd outgrown. Just as a big-name restaurant offers her a dream job on Easter morning, she must choose between her old ambitions and Cole, and she finds a way to stay, reopening the diner with him cheering her on at sunrise.

When big-city pastry chef Maddie Reyes inherits her late grandmother's struggling bakery in tiny Larkspur, Kansas, she plans to sell it quickly, but the town's beloved Easter Bake-Off is only a week away and the bakery is expected to enter. Her grandmother's rival, a stubborn local farmer and egg-supplier named Jake Holloway, reluctantly agrees to help her, mostly because he's secretly been in charge of the town's Easter festival since his own father passed. Between runaway lambs, a flooded church basement, and a hilariously botched attempt at 200 hand-decorated eggs, Maddie and Jake go from bickering to bonding. Just as sparks fly during an after-hours egg-dyeing session, Maddie discovers a sales offer from a developer that Jake thinks she's already accepted. Heartbroken, she nearly leaves, but a handwritten recipe card from her grandmother convinces her to stay, and she wins the Bake-Off, tears up the offer, and shares a sunrise Easter kiss with Jake in the middle of a blooming wildflower field.
